page.layout: 1 running head at top centre: "GRAMMATICA", with page number "250" at the top left. Below it, one full-width text block of italic Latin, then a centred heading "HOPHAL.", a subheading, and two tables of Hebrew verb forms (singular and plural), each with person labels. Then a second centred subheading with a further table (two columns: plural and singular). Then italic Latin lines, the closing line "Reliqua futuro secundo carent.", and at the right bottom the catchword "Verba".

p.i: Iephykkád, tephykkád, tephykkád, tephykkedí, aphykkád. Iephykkedú, te-phykkádna, nephykkád.
Iophkád, tophkád, tophkád, tophke-dí, ophkád. Iophkedú, tophkádna, toph-kedú, tophkádnu, nophkád.

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points are copied from the scan and are not fully certain, especially the dagesh and shewa marks in the tables; those lines are marked [?]. The Hebrew in the two-column future table is read in the printed order (2.M. and 2.F. forms), with the Hebrew forms of the Hophal future (הָפְקַד, הָפְקְּדוּ, הָפְקַדְנָה, הָפְקְּדִי) partly illegible in detail, and their pointing has not been checked letter by letter. The Latin italic lines are read as printed, with the line-end hyphens kept. The word "Verba" at the bottom right is treated as a catchword.
